analysis.lean: No real edge on the side or total: the blended projection (DEN +7.4, total 235.9) is almost exactly the market (DEN -7.5, 236.5), so this is a pass or a very small GSW +7.5 lean at best.
why: Our rating-based margin is DEN +7.0 and the blend is +7.4, against a -7.5 line. The 0.1-point gap is far too small to act on.
The projected total is 232.8 (blend 235.9) against 236.5. That is 0.6 under the market after blending, within noise, so total_adj stays 0.

The samples are tiny: GSW has 3 games and DEN has 2. The ratings are shrunk toward average (GSW net -3.1, DEN +1.6) even though GSW's raw numbers are ugly (123.0 allowed per game, 0.617 opponent eFG).
Both teams are on 1 day of rest, so there is no rest mismatch to justify moving the line.
The shot-profile matchup favors DEN (1.17 expected points per shot vs GSW's 1.076, league 1.084). That is a small-sample estimate, and the market likely already prices DEN's edge.
risks: DEN's 84-96 loss at OKC and 141-135 win over NOP show how noisy 2 games are, so the ratings could be off in either direction.
Santos is questionable and Diallo and Cameron Johnson are doubtful. The rotation could change late, and the line may move on that news.
GSW's last-5 net rating is -11.1, but with 3 games that is just the whole sample, not a separate trend.
matchups: GSW allows a high rate of above-break threes and rim shots; DEN takes 30% of its shots at the rim and Jokic is 114/158 there on the season (zone data, small sample).
Draymond Green and Al Horford score very little (3.5 and 1.5 per game), so GSW's offense depends on Curry, Lendeborg and Podziemski (from the data, not memory).
verify: Confirm whether Santos plays (questionable, left knee tendinitis). Williams and Bassey are listed probable.
Confirm Diallo and Johnson are out for DEN (both doubtful).
Check the line and total again near tip; the packet has no moneyline for either side.
Check whether Curry has any minutes limit; he averages only 25.5 minutes over 3 games, and the packet does not say why.
